day12.title: Building a Semantic Search API with Python & TF-IDF
day12.summary: Build a FastAPI service that ranks documents by semantic similarity using TF-IDF vectors and cosine distance — the same math powering search inside Notion, Algolia, and early Google.
day12.why: Recruiters hiring for AI-adjacent backend roles want to see you reason about text-as-vectors, not just call an OpenAI endpoint. TF-IDF is the foundation every RAG and embedding system builds on. Shipping this proves you understand retrieval from first principles.
requirements: A FastAPI app exposing GET /search?q=<query> returning ranked document titles and scores.
Implement TF-IDF vectorization from scratch in Python (no sklearn for the vectorizer — numpy is fine).
Return top 5 matches ranked by cosine similarity, descending.
Include a /health endpoint and a sample corpus of at least 20 documents.
Commit with a clear message; the README must show a curl example and sample output.
hints: Tokenize by lowercase split, strip punctuation, remove stopwords.
IDF = log(N / (1 + df_t)). The +1 smooths terms unique to one doc.
Cosine similarity = dot(a,b) / (||a|| * ||b||). numpy.dot and numpy.linalg.norm do the heavy lifting.
Cache the IDF vector at startup — recompute per query is wasteful.
day12.recruiterNote: Semantic search is one of the most asked-about skills in AI-backend JDs this quarter. A clean TF-IDF implementation — with tests and a deployed endpoint — is a portfolio piece that opens interview doors at product companies building RAG.

days.title: CLI Pomodoro Timer with Desktop Notifications
days.summary: Build a cross-platform command line pomodoro timer with customizable work/rest intervals, terminal progress animation, and desktop notifications.
days.why: A clean CLI utility demonstrates fundamental OS interaction, timers, state management, and clear terminal UX.
requirements: Custom work and break durations via CLI flags (--work, --break).
Live terminal progress bar or ASCII countdown display.
Desktop notification on timer completion.
Audio chime or bell alert when session finishes.
Clean documentation with installation and CLI usage instructions.
hints: Use argparse/commander for argument parsing.
Terminal ANSI escape codes allow in-place redraws of progress bars.
Test audio chimes gracefully across different terminal environments.
days.recruiterNote: Demonstrates clean code organization, CLI parsing, and asynchronous timer controls in core language runtime.

days.title: Markdown Note Taker with Live HTML Preview
days.summary: Build a web-based Markdown note editor with real-time preview rendering, local storage auto-saving, and syntax highlighting.
days.why: DOM manipulation, reactive state synchronization, and client-side data persistence are core full-stack foundations.
requirements: Split view with Markdown editor on left and live HTML on right.
Debounced auto-save to browser localStorage.
Support for code block syntax highlighting and GFM task lists.
Export note to raw .md or .html file.
Responsive layout supporting dark and light themes.
hints: Use marked.js or remark for fast markdown parsing.
Debounce auto-save by 300ms to avoid thrashing localStorage.
Sanitize rendered HTML to prevent XSS vulnerabilities.
days.recruiterNote: Shows strong client-side state handling, performance considerations, and security awareness with raw user input.

days.title: Weather CLI & API Wrapper with Multi-City Forecasts
days.summary: Integrate with OpenWeatherMap API to fetch current weather and 5-day forecasts with formatted ASCII charts and memory caching.
days.why: Interfacing with external third-party REST APIs, error handling, rate limiting, and output formatting are daily developer tasks.
requirements: Fetch weather by city name or geographic coordinates.
Display current temperature, humidity, wind, and weather condition.
In-memory cache with 10-minute TTL to reduce redundant API calls.
Formatted terminal ASCII output or colored JSON.
Graceful handling for invalid city names or network timeouts.
hints: Check response status codes and return user-friendly errors.
Use absolute temperature conversions (Kelvin to Celsius/Fahrenheit).
Store API keys safely in environment variables.
days.recruiterNote: Proves ability to work with REST endpoints, env secrets, and client-side caching strategies.

days.title: Expense Splitter API & Bill Calculation Engine
days.summary: Design a REST API to divide group expenses with unequal split ratios, tip percentages, and debt-simplification matrix logic.
days.why: Financial logic requires precise arithmetic calculation, data modeling for multi-user transactions, and debt minimization algorithms.
requirements: POST /expenses to record a group expense among members.
Support equal, percentage-based, and exact amount splits.
Debt simplification algorithm to minimize total transaction count.
GET /balances returning net owe/owed amounts per person.
Comprehensive unit tests covering edge cases and round-offs.
hints: Avoid floating point inaccuracies by calculating in cents or using Decimal types.
Graph modeling helps reduce N-way debts to minimal transfers.
Ensure total split percentages sum to exactly 100%.
days.recruiterNote: Algorithm design and debt minimization logic demonstrate mathematical precision and clean domain modeling.

days.title: High-Performance URL Shortener Service
days.summary: Build a URL shortener with Base62 encoding, custom aliases, click analytics tracking, and Redis caching.
days.why: URL shorteners are classic system design interview problems testing database indexing, caching, and redirection logic.
requirements: POST /shorten generating a 6-character Base62 hash or custom alias.
GET /:code redirecting with HTTP 302 and incrementing click count.
Redis cache layer for hot short URLs.
Analytics endpoint GET /analytics/:code returning total clicks and timestamps.
Rate limit creation endpoints to prevent spam.
hints: Base62 encoding derived from auto-increment IDs prevents hash collisions.
HTTP 302 Found ensures click analytics are counted on every hit.
Expire unaccessed URLs after a configurable retention period.
days.recruiterNote: A staple system design project showcasing caching, encoding algorithms, and high-frequency redirection mechanics.

days.title: Realtime Multi-Room Chat with WebSockets
days.summary: Develop a real-time multi-room messaging app using Socket.io or WebSockets with typing indicators and online user presence.
days.why: Event-driven bi-directional communication is necessary for collaborative apps, live feeds, and real-time dashboards.
requirements: Join/leave rooms dynamically without reconnecting the socket.
Real-time broadcasting of text messages and typing indicators.
Live user count and active participant list per room.
Message history persistence in SQLite or PostgreSQL.
Auto-reconnect handling on unexpected network disconnects.
hints: Acknowledge socket events on receipt for reliable delivery.
Sanitize message content before broadcasting.
Debounce 'user typing' events to avoid flooding sockets.
days.recruiterNote: Real-time networking and socket event handling demonstrate readiness for collaborative web software engineering.

days.title: Stateless Authentication Engine with JWT & Refresh Tokens
days.summary: Implement secure user registration, password hashing with bcrypt, JWT access token issuance, and HTTP-only cookie refresh rotation.
days.why: Authentication is mandatory in every production API. Secure token management prevents token theft and replay attacks.
requirements: POST /auth/register with password strength validation and bcrypt hashing.
POST /auth/login issuing short-lived JWT access token and secure refresh cookie.
POST /auth/refresh rotation issuing new token pair and revoking old refresh token.
Protected route middleware verifying Bearer tokens.
Comprehensive unit tests for expired or tampered tokens.
hints: Keep access tokens short-lived (15 mins) and refresh tokens longer (7 days).
Set HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, and Secure flags on refresh cookies.
Store refresh token hashes in DB to enable global logout.
days.recruiterNote: Shows strong security foundation, understanding of cryptographically signed tokens, and token lifecycle management.

days.title: Distributed Background Job Queue & Task Worker
days.summary: Build a producer-consumer job queue using Redis/BullMQ or Python Celery to process heavy background tasks asynchronously.
days.why: Offloading long-running tasks from the HTTP request cycle is critical for API responsiveness and system reliability.
requirements: POST /jobs to enqueue tasks (e.g. image resizing or PDF generation).
Worker process consuming jobs from queue with concurrency controls.
Exponential backoff retry mechanism for failed jobs.
Job status endpoint GET /jobs/:id returning pending/processing/completed state.
Dead-letter queue (DLQ) for permanently failed tasks.
hints: Keep HTTP response fast by returning 202 Accepted with job ID.
Ensure job processing logic is idempotent.
Use Redis transactions or Lua scripts for atomic queue operations.
days.recruiterNote: Demonstrates understanding of asynchronous architecture, queue workers, and failure handling patterns.

days.title: Token Bucket API Rate Limiter Middleware
days.summary: Implement a sliding window or token bucket rate limiter in Go/Node/Python using Redis to protect APIs against abusive traffic.
days.why: Rate limiting is critical for service availability, DDoS mitigation, and monetized API tiering.
requirements: Configurable rate limits (e.g. 10 requests per minute per IP or API key).
HTTP response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response on limit breach.
Redis atomic operations for distributed consistency across multiple API instances.
Bypass mechanism for internal admin keys.
hints: Sliding window log algorithm avoids bursts at boundary windows.
Execute Redis commands inside pipeline/multi to reduce network roundtrips.
Set TTL on Redis keys equal to the rate limit window duration.
days.recruiterNote: Proves ability to protect production services against overload using distributed Redis primitives.

days.title: S3-Compatible Cloud File Upload Service with Signed URLs
days.summary: Build a file upload service using AWS S3 / MinIO signed pre-uploaded URLs, thumbnail generation, and mime-type validation.
days.why: Direct-to-cloud signed uploads keep backend servers lean by avoiding handling binary file streams directly.
requirements: POST /uploads/presign generating short-lived S3 pre-signed upload URL.
Client uploads directly to storage bucket without hitting application server.
Image dimension and mime-type magic bytes verification worker.
Image thumbnail generation background task.
GET /files/:id returning metadata and secure download URL.
hints: Validate file extension AND magic byte header in uploaded files.
Set pre-signed URL expiration to 15 minutes max.
Use S3 lifecycle rules to auto-clean incomplete multipart uploads.
days.recruiterNote: Direct-to-S3 signed URL uploads are industry standard for scalable media handling.

days.title: RESTful CRUD API with Offset & Cursor Pagination
days.summary: Build a clean RESTful API with PostgreSQL/SQLite featuring both page-based offset and keyset/cursor pagination, sorting, and field filtering.
days.why: Efficient database query pagination prevents memory overflow and keeps API responses snappy as table sizes grow.
requirements: GET /items supporting page & limit (offset) AND cursor-based pagination.
Dynamic column sorting (?sort=-created_at) and filtering (?category=tech).
Include total records, page count, and next/prev cursor links in response metadata.
SQL indexing on filtered and sorted columns to ensure O(log N) queries.
Comprehensive test suite verifying pagination boundaries.
hints: Offset pagination degrades on large tables; cursor pagination using ID/timestamp stays fast.
Always sanitize dynamic sort parameters to prevent SQL injection.
Enforce maximum page size limit (e.g., max 100 items per request).
days.recruiterNote: Understanding offset vs cursor pagination trade-offs is a hallmark of senior backend engineering practice.

days.summary: Build a FastAPI service that ranks documents by semantic similarity using TF-IDF vectors and cosine distance — the same math powering search inside Notion, Algolia, and early Google.
days.why: Recruiters hiring for AI-adjacent backend roles want to see you reason about text-as-vectors, not just call an OpenAI endpoint. TF-IDF is the foundation every RAG and embedding system builds on. Shipping this proves you understand retrieval from first principles.
requirements: A FastAPI app exposing GET /search?q=<query> returning ranked document titles and scores.
Implement TF-IDF vectorization from scratch in Python (no sklearn for the vectorizer — numpy is fine).
Return top 5 matches ranked by cosine similarity, descending.
Include a /health endpoint and a sample corpus of at least 20 documents.
Commit with a clear message; the README must show a curl example and sample output.
hints: Tokenize by lowercase split, strip punctuation, remove stopwords.
IDF = log(N / (1 + df_t)). The +1 smooths terms unique to one doc.
Cosine similarity = dot(a,b) / (||a|| * ||b||). numpy.dot and numpy.linalg.norm do the heavy lifting.
Cache the IDF vector at startup — recompute per query is wasteful.
days.recruiterNote: Semantic search is one of the most asked-about skills in AI-backend JDs this quarter. A clean TF-IDF implementation — with tests and a deployed endpoint — is a portfolio piece that opens interview doors at product companies building RAG.

days.title: Day 13: Redis In-Memory Cache Layer for Heavy Database Queries
days.summary: Implement a Cache-Aside and Write-Through caching layer with Redis to drastically reduce database latency for frequent read queries.
days.why: Caching is essential for high-throughput microservices handling millions of daily reads.
requirements: Cache read results in Redis with configurable TTL.
Implement Cache-Aside pattern for database reads.
Invalidate or update cache entries on data mutation (Write-Through).
Include fallback handling when Redis connection fails.
Benchmark response time improvements with and without cache.
hints: Use key prefixing for namespace separation.
Set jitter on TTL to prevent cache stampede.
Monitor cache hit/miss ratio.
days.recruiterNote: Caching pattern implementation shows senior backend architecture understanding.

days.title: Day 14: Multi-Stage Dockerization of Node.js & React Applications
days.summary: Create slim, secure Docker images using multi-stage builds, non-root user execution, and layer optimization.
days.why: Containerization is the standard packaging mechanism for modern cloud-native deployments.
requirements: Multi-stage Dockerfile separating build dependencies from runtime artifact.
Ensure final image size is under 150MB using Alpine/Distroless base.
Run application under a non-root user for container security.
Configure .dockerignore to exclude node_modules and build logs.
Docker Compose configuration with database service and volume persistence.
hints: Leverage Docker build cache by copying package.json before source files.
Use healthcheck instructions in compose file.
days.recruiterNote: Production-ready Dockerfiles are essential for DevOps and cloud development roles.

days.title: Day 15: Local Vector Database Search with ChromaDB & Embeddings
days.summary: Build a document semantic search service by storing text chunks and vector embeddings in ChromaDB or Qdrant.
days.why: Vector databases form the backbone of modern AI search, memory, and RAG pipelines.
requirements: Chunk long text documents with overlapping character windows.
Generate text embeddings using OpenAI or HuggingFace local models.
Store chunks and metadata in ChromaDB vector collection.
Expose search API returning top-K relevant chunks with similarity distance.
Interactive UI or CLI to query the vector database.
hints: Chunk size 500 characters with 50 overlap is a good baseline.
Normalize query strings before generating query embedding.
days.recruiterNote: Vector database integration demonstrates hands-on competency in modern AI engineering.

days.title: Day 16: PostgreSQL Indexing, Query Tuning & EXPLAIN ANALYZE
days.summary: Diagnose slow SQL queries, create B-tree, Hash, and GIN indexes, and analyze execution plans with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
days.why: Database query optimization is the single most effective way to improve application performance under load.
requirements: Seed a PostgreSQL database with 500,000 dummy records.
Identify sequential table scans on unindexed search queries.
Apply B-tree and Composite indexes to reduce execution time from >500ms to <5ms.
GIN index for JSONB column key-value queries.
Document Before/After query plans using EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS).
hints: Avoid over-indexing as it slows down write operations.
Composite index column order matters (most selective column first).
days.recruiterNote: Query optimization experience sets candidate apart in technical backend interviews.

days.title: Day 17: CI/CD Pipeline with GitHub Actions & Automated Testing
days.summary: Build an automated CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions that runs linters, unit tests, security audits, and builds Docker artifacts.
days.why: Automated delivery pipelines ensure code quality and prevent broken builds from hitting production.
requirements: GitHub Actions workflow triggered on pull requests and pushes to main.
Parallel jobs for linting, type checking, and test execution.
Build and tag Docker image on successful tests.
Cache npm/pip dependencies to reduce pipeline execution time.
Generate test coverage report badge in README.
hints: Use matrix builds to test across multiple Node/Python versions.
Store registry credentials in GitHub Encrypted Secrets.
days.recruiterNote: Demonstrates practical automation and continuous integration discipline.

days.title: Day 18: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Bot with Gemini API
days.summary: Combine vector search retrieval with Gemini API prompt engineering to answer context-grounded questions over custom PDF/text files.
days.why: RAG is the dominant enterprise architecture for grounding LLMs on proprietary data without hallucinations.
requirements: Parse PDF/text upload into vector embeddings.
Retrieve top 3 context passages for incoming user query.
Construct grounded system prompt passing context snippets to Gemini model.
Streaming text response back to web client.
Provide source citations (page/document name) in the generated response.
hints: Instruct model to explicitly state 'I don't know' if context is insufficient.
Stream chunks using server-sent events or WebSocket.
days.recruiterNote: RAG is the #1 requested capability in AI product company job descriptions.

days.title: Day 19: ETL Data Pipeline with Pandas & Apache Airflow DAG
days.summary: Design an automated ETL pipeline that ingests raw CSV sales data, cleans null values, aggregates metrics, and loads into PostgreSQL.
days.why: Data engineering pipelines ensure clean, timely data for downstream analytics and machine learning models.
requirements: Extract raw sales data from external CSV or REST endpoint.
Transform data using Pandas: clean nulls, format timestamps, calculate daily totals.
Load transformed records into PostgreSQL warehouse schema.
Define Apache Airflow DAG scheduled to run daily with retries.
Data validation checks verifying row counts and non-null constraints.
hints: Use Airflow PostgresOperator for loading steps.
Log data quality failures to slack or alert channel.
days.recruiterNote: Shows core data engineering capabilities in data transformation and orchestration.

days.title: Day 20: GraphQL API Server with DataLoader Batching
days.summary: Build a GraphQL API server with Apollo/GraphQL-Yoga featuring nested resolvers, schema design, and DataLoader to solve N+1 query problems.
days.why: GraphQL gives frontend clients precise data fetching control while DataLoader solves database performance bottlenecks.
requirements: GraphQL schema defining Types, Queries, Mutations, and Inputs.
Resolver implementation for nested relational data (Authors -> Books).
Implement DataLoader to batch and cache nested database queries.
GraphQL Playground UI enabled for interactive testing.
Input validation and custom GraphQL error formatting.
hints: DataLoader batches all key lookups within a single event loop tick.
Avoid deep query nesting attacks with depth limiters.
days.recruiterNote: Proves ability to build efficient, flexible GraphQL APIs without N+1 query performance regressions.

days.title: Day 21: Prometheus Metrics & Grafana Observability Dashboard
days.summary: Instrument an HTTP application with Prometheus RED metrics (Rate, Errors, Duration) and visualize real-time graphs in Grafana.
days.why: Observability enables quick detection and debugging of outages before users notice.
requirements: Expose /metrics endpoint in application using client library (prom-client/prometheus_client).
Track HTTP request count by route and status code counter.
Histogram tracking HTTP request duration latency distribution.
Prometheus server configuration scraping application target.
Grafana dashboard showing ops metrics (RPS, 5xx error rate, p95 latency).
hints: Use buckets tuned for web request latencies (10ms to 5s).
Label cardinality should be kept low — do not put user IDs in labels.
days.recruiterNote: Instrumenting application metrics is crucial for site reliability and cloud platform engineering.

days.title: Day 22: Event-Driven Message Streaming with Apache Kafka
days.summary: Set up a Kafka cluster producing and consuming order processing events with consumer groups and at-least-once delivery semantics.
days.why: Event streaming allows microservices to decouple and communicate asynchronously at massive scale.
requirements: Kafka topic configured with multiple partitions.
Producer publishing order-created events with partitioning keys.
Consumer group with multiple workers balancing partition consumption.
Handle offset commits explicitly to guarantee message processing.
Graceful shutdown handling flushing pending offsets.
hints: Use order ID as key to guarantee ordering within partition.
Set consumer session timeout appropriately for heavy processing.
days.recruiterNote: Kafka skills are highly sought after for distributed systems and fintech backend roles.

days.title: Day 23: Sentiment Classification Model with PyTorch & HuggingFace
days.summary: Fine-tune a DistilBERT transformer model on movie or product reviews to classify positive/negative sentiment.
days.why: Understanding deep learning NLP pipelines from tokenization to model inference is foundational for ML engineers.
requirements: Load and preprocess text dataset using HuggingFace Datasets.
Tokenize inputs with DistilBERT tokenizer.
Fine-tune PyTorch model for binary sequence classification.
Evaluate accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score on test set.
Export fine-tuned model weights and create inference function.
hints: Use mixed precision training (fp16) to speed up GPU training.
Set random seeds for reproducible evaluation results.
days.recruiterNote: Demonstrates practical machine learning training, evaluation, and model deployment workflow.

days.title: Day 24: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) & Permission Guard Middleware
days.summary: Design a granular RBAC middleware supporting Roles (Admin, Editor, Viewer) and specific Scopes (posts:read, posts:write).
days.why: Enterprise platforms require strict security boundaries restricting access based on user authorization roles.
requirements: Database schema for Users, Roles, Permissions, and UserRoles mapping.
Middleware checking route authorization requirement against user token roles.
Hierarchical permission inheritance (Admin inherits Editor permissions).
API endpoints demonstrating allowed vs 403 Forbidden access.
Unit tests verifying role boundary restrictions.
hints: Cache user roles in request context or JWT claims to avoid DB query per request.
Keep permission names explicit (e.g. org:billing:manage).
days.recruiterNote: Security and access control design is vital for multi-tenant enterprise software.

days.title: Day 25: Terraform Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for AWS / GCP
days.summary: Provision a VPC, public/private subnets, storage bucket, and serverless Cloud Run / ECS instance using declarative Terraform scripts.
days.why: Infrastructure as Code allows teams to version control, review, and replicate cloud environments reliably.
requirements: Modularized Terraform configuration (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf).
Provision networking VPC with isolated subnets.
Deploy cloud bucket with encryption and public access block enabled.
Remote state storage configuration with state locking.
Clean terraform plan and terraform apply workflow.
hints: Never commit secrets or state files to Git repository.
Use variables for region and environment naming.
days.recruiterNote: IaC proficiency with Terraform is mandatory for modern cloud infrastructure roles.

days.title: Day 26: Automated AI Code Reviewer Bot using Gemini API
days.summary: Build a GitHub webhook integration or CLI tool that analyzes code diffs using Gemini API and leaves constructive code review comments.
days.why: AI-assisted developer tooling speeds up pull request reviews and catches syntax bugs automatically.
requirements: Parse git diff or GitHub PR pull request payload.
Send code diff to Gemini API with targeted code review prompt.
Categorize feedback into Security, Performance, and Style suggestions.
Post formatted markdown review comment back to GitHub PR API.
Ignore autogenerated files and locks.
hints: Format prompt with structured output JSON schema.
Trimming whitespace in git diff reduces API token costs.
days.recruiterNote: Exhibits creative application of AI models to developer workflow automation.

days.title: Day 27: Feature Flag Engine with Realtime Dynamic Rollouts
days.summary: Build a feature flagging library allowing percentage-based rollouts, user targeting rules, and instant toggle changes without redeploying code.
days.why: Feature flags facilitate continuous deployment, A/B testing, and instant kill-switches for faulty features.
requirements: Admin API to create/update feature flags and targeting rules.
Consistent hashing algorithm for user ID percentage rollouts (e.g., 20% of users).
Client SDK/helper function evaluating flag state in <1ms.
Realtime update propagation via SSE or WebSocket.
Audit log recording flag state changes.
hints: Use MurmurHash3 on userId + flagKey to produce deterministic percentages.
Cache flag rules in memory locally.
days.recruiterNote: Feature flag system design highlights software reliability and deployment strategy awareness.

days.title: Day 28: Web Scraping Data Pipeline with Playwright & BeautifulSoup
days.summary: Scrape dynamic rendered web pages using Playwright browser automation, extract structured records, and handle pagination & anti-bot throttling.
days.why: Web data extraction fuels competitive intelligence, price tracking, and training data collection.
requirements: Headless browser navigation handling SPA JavaScript rendering.
Extract structured product listings (title, price, availability, rating).
Handle multi-page pagination and lazy loading scroll triggers.
Rate limiting and request delay jitter to avoid triggering anti-bot blocks.
Output clean structured JSON or CSV dataset.
hints: Wait for specific selector state before extracting text.
Use User-Agent header rotation.
days.recruiterNote: Data harvesting skills are key for data engineering and scraping automation positions.

days.title: Day 29: Microservices Inter-Service Communication with gRPC & Protocol Buffers
days.summary: Define .proto schemas and implement high-performance gRPC client and server services in Go/Node with binary serialization.
days.why: gRPC delivers up to 10x faster performance than REST JSON for internal microservices communication.
requirements: Define Protocol Buffer service schema with messages and RPC methods.
Compile .proto to language-specific stubs.
Server implementation handling Unary and Server Streaming RPC calls.
Client implementation with connection pooling and deadline timeouts.
gRPC metadata headers for authentication.
hints: Always specify explicit deadlines/timeouts on client calls.
Use protoc plugins for code generation.
days.recruiterNote: gRPC and Protobuf mastery demonstrates readiness for high-throughput distributed architectures.

days.title: Day 30: Server-Sent Events (SSE) Real-Time Notification Feed
days.summary: Implement an SSE endpoint streaming live system events and notifications from backend to browser with automatic reconnection handling.
days.why: SSE provides lightweight, unidirectional real-time updates over standard HTTP without WebSocket overhead.
requirements: GET /events endpoint with Content-Type: text/event-stream headers.
Keep-alive heartbeats to prevent connection drops by proxies.
Event ID tracking allowing client to resume missed events via Last-Event-ID header.
Frontend EventSource client rendering live toast notifications.
Graceful disconnection handling on server shutdown.
hints: Disable HTTP response buffering in Nginx/Express.
Format events with standard 'event:', 'data:', and 'id:' lines.
days.recruiterNote: Understanding lightweight real-time protocols like SSE shows good architecture judgment.

days.title: Day 31: Kubernetes Pod Deployment, Services & Ingress Setup
days.summary: Deploy a web app to a local Minikube/K3s Kubernetes cluster using Deployment, ClusterIP Service, ConfigMap, and Ingress manifests.
days.why: Kubernetes is the industry standard container orchestrator for scaling microservices in production.
requirements: Kubernetes Deployment manifest specifying 3 replicas and rolling update strategy.
ConfigMap and Secret mounted into pod environment variables.
Service manifest exposing cluster internal endpoint.
Ingress routing path-based traffic to backend service.
Liveness and Readiness probe configurations checking /health route.
hints: Readiness probes prevent traffic routing to booting pods.
Set resource request and limits on CPU and memory.
days.recruiterNote: Kubernetes deployment and manifest authorship is a core DevOps requirement.

days.title: Day 32: LLM Fine-Tuning with LoRA on Custom Domain Dataset
days.summary: Fine-tune a lightweight LLM (Llama-3-8B or Mistral-7B) using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT/LoRA) on custom domain Q&A data.
days.why: Fine-tuning adapts open models to specialized domain terminology and stylistic constraints efficiently.
requirements: Prepare instruction-tuning dataset in JSONL format.
Configure LoRA parameters (r=8, alpha=16, target_modules).
Execute training loop using HuggingFace SFTTrainer or Unsloth.
Track training loss curves and perplexity.
Evaluate qualitative output before vs after fine-tuning.
hints: Use 4-bit quantization (QLoRA) to reduce GPU memory requirements.
Format prompt template consistently during training and inference.
days.recruiterNote: Hands-on LLM fine-tuning experience is in high demand across AI engineering teams.

days.title: Day 33: Payment Gateway Integration with Stripe Webhooks
